requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) configured as DNS resolver answering inventory.internal with node2's address on the shared 10.100.232.0/24 network
requirements.summary: VyOS static-host-mapping for inventory.internal -> 10.100.232.11 was applied and committed/saved; dig from node1 and from clients confirms resolution. Config was applied via manual validation (cmd-17d7c20f5f8c469b/cmd-80215e19446840bc) and then confirmed reproducible/applied through the Ansible playbook (cmd-13bbd69976c54166). Configuration persisted and worked identically after a full node1 reboot (cmd-44bcf48e207440e4).

requirements.requirement: node1 forwards all other DNS queries upstream
requirements.summary: VyOS 'service dns forwarding' with name-server 10.100.232.1 configured; dig for example.com against node1 resolves correctly both before and after the node1 restart.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to resolve through node1
requirements.summary: resolvconf head override pointing at 10.100.232.10 installed via the Ansible playbook on both clients; getent hosts confirms inventory.internal and a public name resolve through node1 both immediately after the playbook run and after independent restarts of node2 and node3.

requirements.requirement: Implementation performed using Ansible from the control node
requirements.summary: An inventory/ansible.cfg/playbook.yml were created on node4 (the designated control node) and ansible-playbook was run against node1/node2/node3, with a subsequent idempotent re-run also completing successfully.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (node1-node4) with pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: For each of node1, node2, node3, and node4, distinct baseline boot_id, a reboot command, a subsequent different boot_id, and post-reboot verification of DNS/resolver functionality (and, for node4, a full successful playbook re-run) are all directly observed in the evidence, matching the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check.

overall_summary: The executor successfully implemented node1 as a VyOS DNS forwarder answering inventory.internal with node2's address and forwarding all other queries upstream, and configured node2/node3 to resolve through node1, all via an Ansible playbook run from the designated control node (node4). Functional verification (dig/getent) confirms correct resolution both immediately after configuration and after each node's individual restart, with idempotent playbook re-runs also succeeding. The mandatory provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was completed for all four managed nodes with clear baseline, restart, changed-boot-identity, and recovery evidence, including a full playbook re-run from node4 after its own reboot.
limitations: The first successful Ansible-driven application of node1's DNS config (cmd-13bbd69976c54166) occurred after the same configuration had already been applied manually via raw SSH; because the VyOS task uses ansible.builtin.raw (which reports changed by default), it cannot be fully distinguished from evidence alone whether the playbook task itself would independently apply the config from a clean state versus reporting changed due to raw-module semantics on an already-configured system.

Systemd 'listening-sockets' hygiene evidence is only available for node1 and node4; node2/node3 listening-socket observations were empty/unavailable both before and after, limiting cross-checking of unexpected service exposure on the Ubuntu clients.

operational_hygiene.summary: The bulk of state-changing commands were clearly tied to necessary prerequisites (SSH key setup for Ansible connectivity to node1/node2/node3) or to applying and verifying the DNS configuration itself. One unnecessary, bounded mutation occurred: the executor wrote /root/.ssh/authorized_keys on node1 (cmd-7bf2d980a3434a23) in an attempt to enable root SSH login, which was refused by sshd (ROOT LOGIN REFUSED, observed in cmd-dda4a11b91eb4aeb) and was then fully reverted (cmd-ef76c8fd24c6474e removed the file) once the executor switched to the working 'vyos' user. Several ansible-playbook and raw-SSH command attempts failed during iterative debugging of quoting/escaping issues (e.g. cmd-69a29de7df044361, cmd-3daa64e0816c40e1, cmd-8db6df840f794991, cmd-5ce7590ffb284467, cmd-8bcdb165f6364a05) but these were re-attempts of the same intended configuration, not divergent or destructive mutations, and did not leave residue. The lifecycle diff between after-prepare and after-executor shows only expected changes (new boot identities from restarts, DNS service now listening on node1, rotated systemd-private temp dirs) with no failed services, no package-health issues, and no unexplained residue.
